NPC by class and level

NPCs

Roll a d20: the number shown or higher saves. Monsters save as warriors of a level equal to their Hit Dice, counting one more die for every four extra hit points or part of four (5+6 Hit Dice saves at level 7). A creature with no intelligence saves at half that level, rounded up, except against poison and death magic. A monster with another class’s abilities may use that class’s rows instead. (DMG p. 65)

Which saving throw to use

When more than one could apply, use the one that comes first in this order (DMG p. 65):

  1. Paralyzation, poison or death magic: any paralyzing attack, any poison, and spells or items that kill outright.
  2. Rod, staff or wand: the powers of those items, unless a save higher on this list applies.
  3. Petrification or polymorph: being turned to stone or polymorphed (but a wand of polymorphing uses the wand save).
  4. Breath weapon: dragon breath and the like.
  5. Spell: any other magical attack, and anything that fits nowhere else.

Rules and sources

Each rule this page uses, where it comes from, and how sure the wording is. Book was read from the 1989 Dungeon Master’s Guide, Chapter 11. Site was read from an online copy of the Monstrous Manual and not checked against a printed book. Judgment is a choice this page makes where the books leave it to the DM.

StepWhat the page doesSourceStatus
Wilderness checkAt the time blocks marked for the terrain, roll 1d10; an encounter happens on the terrain’s chance or less. +1 if patrolled or sparsely settled, +2 if heavily populated.DMG Table 56, p. 101Book
Dungeon checkRoll 1d10 once an hour; encounter on a 1. You can raise the chance or check more often.DMG p. 101Book
Declared encounter“Skip the check” goes straight to the monster.DMG p. 101, “Is This Encounter Necessary?”Book
Monster, automatic listd100: 01–70 common, 71–90 uncommon, 91–97 rare, 98–00 very rare. One monster is then picked with equal chance from that group.DMG p. 97–98, percentile tableBook for the percentages. Judgment: the book has the DM choose which monsters go on a table; this page lists every one that fits.
Empty frequency groupIf no monster of the rolled frequency fits, the nearest group that has monsters is used, and the result says so.Not coveredJudgment
Monster, 2–20 table1d8 + 1d12 against a table of nineteen slots with the book’s frequency for each slot. Two entries in one slot have a 50% chance each.DMG Table 54, p. 98Book
Unique monstersNever placed on a table.DMG p. 97Book
Terrain matchingThe Monstrous Manual’s terrain wording is matched to the ten terrain types of Table 56, plus dungeon and fresh water. The book’s own wording is shown on every result.Monstrous Manual; DMG Table 56Judgment
“Any” and “Any land”Counted for every land terrain including arctic, but not ocean. Plain “Any” also counts for dungeons.Judgment
ClimateA monster with a stated climate (tropical, temperate and so on) only appears when the chosen climate matches. A range such as “tropical and temperate” includes the climates between.Judgment
HumansThe book gives humans a frequency but no terrain. With the box ticked, sailors, fishermen and pirates can appear at sea and all other humans on any land terrain. Humans are not placed in dungeons unless you add them.Judgment
DinosaursLeft out of random encounters altogether, at your request. The DMG lists Prehistoric as its own kind of terrain. You can still add a dinosaur to a place on the Tables page.DMG p. 99, terrain listJudgment
Domestic animalsDraft, riding and war horses, ponies, mules, war dogs, cattle and sheep have a frequency and “any land” terrain in the book, so they used to come up as common wilderness encounters. They are left out of random encounters. Wild horses, wild dogs, camels and other herd animals are unaffected. You can still add any of them to a place on the Tables page.My choiceJudgment
Night creatures by dayWith the box ticked, monsters whose Active line reads Night, Nocturnal, Darkness or similar are left out of the three daytime checks (7–10 a.m., 11 a.m.–2 p.m., 3–6 p.m.). Monsters active by day, at any time, at dawn or dusk, or with no entry can appear at any hour. Your own 2–20 tables and monsters you added by hand are never filtered. The book has no such rule for encounter checks.Monstrous Manual, Activity CycleJudgment
Dungeon dwellersAny monster whose terrain mentions subterranean, caves, ruins or similar, plus monsters found on “any land” (orcs, goblins, kobolds and the like), apart from horses, herd animals and elephants.Monstrous ManualJudgment
Birds, fish, insects, ordinary animalsThe book’s grouped tables give no frequency or terrain, so these never appear unless you add them on the Tables page.Monstrous ManualSite
Dungeon levelBy XP value: 1–20 level 1; 21–50 level 2; 51–150 level 3; 151–250 level 4; 251–500 level 5; 501–1,000 level 6; 1,001–3,000 level 7; 3,001–5,500 level 8; 5,501–10,000 level 9; 10,001+ level 10.DMG Table 55, p. 99Book
Other dungeon levelsA monster one level away is one step rarer (common becomes uncommon), two levels away two steps, and so on until it drops off.DMG p. 99Book
XP given as a listWhen XP depends on Hit Dice or rank, the first listed value (the ordinary creature) sets the dungeon level.Judgment
Treasure typesTable 84, read from the book: for each column a percentage roll, then the amount. Columns with no percentage are always present. Each gem is rolled on Table 85, with a 10% chance of a Table 86 variation; each art object on Table 87; each magical item on Table 88 and its own table.DMG pp. 133–140, Tables 84–110Book
Treasure diceThe book prints amounts as ranges. This page rolls the dice that give exactly that range: 200–2,000 as 2d10 × 100, 3–18 as 3d6, and so on. The dice used are shown on every roll.My reading of Table 84 and 87Judgment
Carried and lair treasureLetters in parentheses on a monster’s Treasure line are lair treasure; the rest may be carried by each monster, so carried types J to Z are rolled once per individual for monsters of semi-intelligence or better. For monsters of animal intelligence or none, the DMG calls these a small lair’s treasure, so they are rolled once for the whole group. Types A to I are always rolled once, as a hoard. A multiplier such as Q×5 is rolled as that type five times; the book only says it marks a large treasure. Conditions such as “magic only” are shown but not applied.Monstrous Manual introduction; DMG p. 133Judgment
Treasure type B, magical itemsThe column reads “Armor Weapon”. It is rolled as one item from Table 88, rolling again until the result is Armor and Shields or Weapons.DMG Table 84Judgment
Items with their own tableMany items carry a small table of their own in their description: which elementals a protection scroll wards against, the bonus of a ring of protection, the size of a bag of holding, the stones in a set of ioun stones, and so on (40 items). The generator now makes that roll and shows the outcome first, with the roll listed among the item’s rolls. Tables used during play are not rolled (wand of wonder, amulet of the planes, mixing potions). The arrow of slaying’s table is the book’s list of sample types. A robe of useful items’ “scroll of one random spell” is left for you to roll with the scroll button.Book
NPC maximum hit points at 1st levelA tick box on the NPC tab (off unless you tick it) makes the NPC’s 1st-level hit die count as its maximum instead of being rolled, a common house rule. The Constitution adjustment is still added, and dice for later levels are rolled as usual. The books roll every die (PHB class hit dice; Table 3).Judgment
NPCs outside the book’s limitsThe NPC tab has a tick box that allows any race in any class with no level limit. The book forbids these (DMG Table 7), so each such NPC carries a note saying so. Everything else is worked out as usual: the class’s own tables for hit points, THAC0, saving throws, spells and skills, with the race’s ability adjustments and thief-skill adjustments. Ability scores are still raised to the class and race minimums and held to the race’s maximums.Judgment
Saving throws tabThe numbers are the saving throw table printed in both books (DMG Table 46, p. 65). Roll a d20: the number shown or higher succeeds. Monsters follow DMG p. 65: a monster saves at a level equal to its Hit Dice, counting one more die for every four extra hit points or part of four (so 5+6 saves at 7th level). A creature with no intelligence (less than animal) saves at half that, rounded up, against everything except poison and death magic. Most monsters use the Warrior table; one with another class’s abilities may use that table, or whichever is better, which is your choice in the “Table to use” box. Picking a monster by name fills in its Hit Dice and intelligence from the Monstrous Manual entry; entries whose Hit Dice are a range or “see below” are left for you to type. Characters can add the Constitution bonus of dwarves, gnomes and halflings against rods, staves, wands and spells (and poison for dwarves and halflings); Wisdom and Dexterity adjustments are shown as notes because they apply only to some attacks. The paralyzation, poison and death column is one number in the book; for a mindless monster the tab shows the full-level number for poison and death and the halved number for paralyzation, which is my reading of “all but poison and death”.Book
Random spellbookThe books give no table for the contents of a found spellbook, so this is my rule: for each spell level the owner can cast, the book holds as many spells as a wizard of that level can memorize (PHB Table 21; one more for a specialist), plus 1d3 extra. Spells are picked at random from the Player’s Handbook list for the level. A specialist’s book has at least one spell of the school at each level and none from the opposition schools. The owner’s Intelligence is not checked, and read magic and detect magic are not forced in. A wizard or bard NPC has a button for the same thing: that book always contains the spells the NPC has memorized, plus 1d3 more per spell level.Judgment
Arachnophobia filterA tick box on the Encounter tab, off by default. When on, random encounters never produce: every monster listed under Spider (gargantuan, giant, hairy, huge, large, phase, sword), every Scorpion (giant, huge, large), the ettercap, drider, manscorpion, neogi and giant tick. It does not touch your own tables on the Tables tab, the Monsters list, or monster descriptions that merely mention spiders (a drow’s pet spiders, for instance). This is a table preference, not a rule from the books.Judgment
Notes tabEvery encounter, day summary, treasure and NPC has a “Keep” button that copies it to the Notes tab, where you can add a note to it. Kept results and the scratch pad are stored by your browser on this computer, for this file in its current folder; they are not written into the file. Moving or renaming the file, using another browser or clearing browsing data hides or removes them, so use “Save a backup” (it downloads one small file) and “Load a backup” to carry them across.—
My spellsThe Spells tab’s “My spells” list (the spells you mark with ☆) is stored with your Notes and is included in the same backup file.——
Monster saving throws, guessedThe Monsters tab works out each monster’s saving throws from its Hit Dice (DMG p. 65). About 190 entries do not give a plain number, and for those the level is a guess, marked “a guess” with the reasoning shown: a range of Hit Dice uses the middle of the range; an entry in hit points is divided by 4½ (the average of a d8); a fraction of a Hit Die uses level 1; a list of alternatives uses the middle one; and where the entry gives nothing usable (“see below”, “varies”), the level is taken from the monster’s THAC0 as 21 minus THAC0. None of these conversions is in the books.Judgment
Dragons by ageOn the Monsters tab a dragon has an age menu. Choosing an age shows that dragon’s figures at that age, all taken from the Monstrous Manual’s tables as recorded in the notes: Hit Dice (the base figure plus the age modifier, −6 at hatchling to +8 at great wyrm), Armor Class, breath weapon damage, the combat modifier added to each physical attack’s damage, magic resistance, fear radius and save modifier, spells, treasure and XP. Two figures are worked out rather than read from the dragon’s entry: THAC0 is the DMG’s creature table (Table 39) for the Hit Dice at that age, which stops improving at 5 for 16 Hit Dice or more; and saving throws are a warrior’s at a level equal to the Hit Dice. Where a dragon’s entry was not recorded in a form the page can read (some spells and treasure lists, the shadow and steel dragons’ breath), it says to see the notes.Book
Town encounters (1st Edition)The Encounter tab’s Town mode uses the City/Town Encounters Matrix from the 1st Edition Dungeon Masters Guide (Appendix C, p. 191), with its day and night columns, its race table for results marked with an asterisk, and its drunk and harlot sub-tables. Each result then makes the rolls its explanation calls for (pp. 191–194): numbers, levels, companions and the percentage chances (knows gossip, already employed, in human form and so on). Where the book gives a range without dice (“2 to 8”), the matching dice are used (2d4). Levels and numbers are as printed, not converted to 2nd Edition. Assassins and monks are 1st Edition classes; their “Make” buttons build stand-ins under 2nd Edition rules, an assassin as a thief and a monk as a fighter or a cleric (your choice of button), and the NPC says so. Town assassins and bards have no level in the book, so a suggested level (d4+4 for assassins, as for the ruffians’ hidden assassin; d6+4 for bards) is put in a box you can change. “Make this NPC” builds the person with the NPC tab’s 2nd Edition rules; a half-orc becomes a human, and a race and class the 2nd Edition book forbids is allowed with a note. The book gives no explanation for peddlers, bards or liches, and its table of magic items carried by townsfolk (p. 194) is not used. The book also says to check every three turns, or as you like, and to ignore a result that makes no sense where the party is; that judgment is left to you.Book
Shop pricesThe Shop tab lists the Player’s Handbook equipment table (312 items) with each item’s weight, and for weapons the size, type, speed, damage and ranges. The price level is my addition: it multiplies every book price (½, ¾, 1½, 2 or your own percentage) to suit a remote village or a city in short supply, and the book price is shown beside it.PHB Tables 44 and 45Book; price levels Judgment
Shop: Rules Cyclopedia notesA few items the PHB lists without explanation carry a short note from the D&D Rules Cyclopedia, marked “Rules Cyclopedia” so you can ignore them.Rules CyclopediaJudgment
Turning undeadThe Saves tab shows PHB Table 61 for one level at a time. Paladins use the column two levels lower, as the table’s note says; the 10–11, 12–13 and 14+ columns are as printed.PHB Table 61, p. 103Book
Monster hit pointsOn the table cards, “Roll” gives each monster 1d8 per Hit Die plus any extra points (4+3 Hit Dice: 4d8+3), at least 1. Entries written as hit points (“2-7 hp”) or as ½ Hit Die (1d4) are rolled as written; a dragon uses the Hit Dice for the age you chose. Anything else you type in yourself.Monstrous Manual (Hit Dice are d8s)Book
Dragon treasureA dragon added to a treasure roll uses the treasure letters for the age chosen on the Monsters tab (Monstrous Manual age table), rolled as its lair hoard.Monstrous Manual, dragon age tablesBook
Magic items tabLists every magic item named in DMG Tables 89–104, 107 and 110 (the ordinary +1, +2… armor and weapons of Tables 105–109 are not separate items), with the same condensed description the treasure roller shows, the XP value printed in the table, and the classes the table names in brackets as able to use it (“Any class” when it names none). The DMG’s general notes for each kind of item (identifying potions, scroll spell failure, command words and so on) are filed with that kind, in italics. As with spells, the descriptions are summaries, not the book’s text.DMG Tables 89–110Book; descriptions summarized
Spell descriptionsEvery wizard and priest spell in the Player’s Handbook (486) has a short description, shown on scrolls, on NPC spell lists and in the Spells tab, which lists them all. The range, components, duration, casting time, area and saving throw are the book’s printed values. The sentence underneath is a condensed summary in my words, not the full text: unusual cases and material components are left out. One entry, Phantasmal Killer, has a misprinted modifier in the book (“+1/”), shown as printed. Forbiddance is missing from the book’s list of spells by sphere; its own entry says Protection, so it is filed there.Summary
ScrollsA spell scroll is a wizard’s on 01–70 and a priest’s on 71–00. Spell levels in a range are rolled with the matching die, for example 2–9 as 1d8+1 (my reading of the range). Each spell is then picked at random from the Player’s Handbook list for its level (my method; the book says only to consult the spell tables), and the level it is cast at is one above the lowest level able to cast it, never below 6th.DMG Table 90, p. 145Book
Armor Class of magical armorShown beside each suit: the armor’s ordinary Armor Class improved by its plus (or worsened by a cursed −1). The ordinary values are from the Player’s Handbook: leather 8; studded leather and ring mail 7; brigandine and scale mail 6; chain mail 5; banded and splint mail 4; plate mail 3; field plate 2; full plate 1; a shield improves each by 1. Dexterity is not included on the Treasure tab.PHB Table 46, p. 75; DMG p. 180Book
NPC: tables usedAbility score effects (PHB Tables 1–6), racial requirements and adjustments (Tables 7–8), class minimums (Table 13), hit dice (Tables 14, 20, 23, 25), spells per level (Tables 17, 18, 21, 24, 32), thieving skills (Tables 26–28, 33), THAC0 (Table 53), saving throws (Table 60), movement (Table 64), spell lists by school and sphere (Appendices 5 and 6), and racial class and level limits (DMG Table 7). All were read from images of your books.PHB; DMG p. 15Book
NPC: ability scoresYour choice of four Player’s Handbook methods: I (3d6 in order), III (3d6 six times, arranged), IV (3d6 twelve times, best six, arranged) or V (4d6 dropping the lowest die, arranged), which is the default. Where the method lets scores be arranged, this page puts the best roll in the class’s most useful ability and works down; that order is my choice. A score below the minimum for the chosen class or race is raised to that minimum, and one above the racial maximum is lowered, so the result is always a legal character. A spellcaster’s Intelligence or Wisdom is also raised, if needed, to the score required for the highest spell level its class table gives at that level (PHB Tables 4 and 24). The book lets a DM raise scores this way only up to 16; a paladin’s Charisma 17 goes past that.PHB pp. 13, 25Judgment
NPC: magical items and treasureFor each kind of item the class may have, a 5% chance per level; a cursed or unusable result is rolled again once. Paladins and rangers use the fighter’s column, druids the cleric’s, bards the thief’s, and specialists the wizard’s (the book lists only the four basic classes). Rolled armor, shields, plain swords and plain weapons are worked into the Armor Class and attack lines; other items are not. “Any” class and race, and the carried treasure types, come from the same pages.Monstrous Manual, Human (Adventurer) and NPC partiesSite
NPC: equipment, spells, skills, alignmentThe books give no roll for these, so this page chooses. Armor follows the Monstrous Manual’s remarks (scale or chain at 1st level, banded or plate after, plate mail and shield from 4th; rangers studded leather; thieves, bards and druids leather). Weapons, alignment and memorised spells are picked at random from what the class allows; wizards are limited by Intelligence and specialists by their opposition schools. Thief and bard skill points are spread at random within the book’s limits. Change anything that does not suit your NPC.My choicesJudgment
NPC: personalityOne general trait on 1d20, one of its five specific traits, and one more characteristic on percentile dice, as in the book’s example. The book stresses that the DM should choose where possible and drop combinations that make no sense.DMG Table 70, p. 114Book
NPC: left outMulti-class and dual-class characters, proficiencies, languages, age, height and weight, followers, spell books, and the saving throw bonuses noted in each NPC’s list (they are stated but not added to the numbers). Rings of protection and similar items are listed but not added to Armor Class.Not included
Item descriptionsThe text under each magical item is a condensed summary of its description in Appendix 3, written for this page by an AI reader working from images of your book. It is not the book’s wording, and numbers can be wrong or missing. Where the book has a sub-table (which giant, how many charges) the summary gives it but the page does not roll it. Check the book before a ruling that matters.DMG pp. 141–186 (summary)Summary
Gem namesThe names and colours are the book’s lists for each class of stone. The book gives no roll for them, so one is picked at random; you can turn this off.DMG p. 134Judgment
Left out of treasureRolling charges, intelligent swords, the creature type for control potions and similar sub-rolls in the item descriptions (the summaries list them for you to roll), and “DM’s Choice” results, which are reported as printed. Platinum or electrum is your choice. Uncut gems (worth 10%) are not rolled.DMG Appendix 3Not included
Ability notesThe notes under each stat block summarise the monster’s description: special attacks and defences, spell-like powers, leaders and lair numbers. They were condensed by an AI reader from the same online copy and shortened again, so numbers can be wrong or missing, and habitat, ecology and appearance are left out. Treat them as reminders and check the book before a ruling that matters.Monstrous Manual (summary)Summary
DragonsXP depends on age and the book gives no roll for a lone dragon’s age, so you choose it on the result. For dungeon lists a dragon is placed as an adult.Monstrous Manual, DragonSite for the XP. Judgment for adult placement.
Number appearingRolled from the monster’s No. Appearing. Where the book prints only a range, the usual dice are inferred (2–8 as 2d4, 2–5 as 1d4+1) and the result says so. If no standard dice fit, every number in the range is equally likely.Monstrous Manual; DMG p. 101–102Site for the numbers. Judgment for inferred dice.
SurpriseEach side rolls 1d10 and is surprised on 3 or less after modifiers.Player’s Handbook; confirmed by youNot read from a book by this page
Surprise modifiersSilenced −2, invisible −2, distinctive odor +2, every 10 members +1, camouflaged −1 to −3; fleeing −2, poor light −1, darkness −4, panicked −2, anticipating attack +2, suspicious +2; rainy −1, heavy fog −2, extremely still +2.DMG Table 57, p. 102Book. Judgment: “every 10 members” is applied as +1 per full ten in the other group.
DistanceBoth surprised 3d6 feet; one surprised 4d6 feet; otherwise smoke or fog 6d6, jungle or dense forest 1d10×10, light forest 2d6×10, scrub 2d12×10, grassland 5d10×10; night or dungeon is limit of sight.DMG Table 58, p. 102Book. Judgment: forest defaults to light forest; terrains not on the table default to limit of sight.
ReactionOptional. 2d10 plus your modifier, read against the party’s attitude.DMG Table 59, p. 103Book

About the monster data

The stat blocks were read page by page from an online copy of the 1993 Monstrous Manual. A second reading of 23 pages matched the first. Where the site itself looks wrong (for example an XP value printed as “3535”) the value is kept as printed and marked “source check”. Half and quarter Hit Dice did not display on the site and are marked where they were filled in.

Two things come from other editions, and both are labelled where they appear: Town mode on the Encounter tab (1st Edition DMG) and a few notes in the Shop (Rules Cyclopedia). Everything else is 2nd Edition.
